title: Ordered versus usual Cech comparison with local module actions
statement: Let $X',T'$ be schemes and $f':X'\to T'$ a morphism. Let $M$ be a module sheaf on $X'$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $W_i$, $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, any finite family of opens. Let $K$ be an integer cochain complex of module sheaves on $T'$ with zero negative terms. Suppose for all nonnegative $p$ and opens $B\subset T'$ there are additive equivalences $a_{p,B}:\Gamma(B,K^p)\simeq\prod_t\Gamma((\bigcap_lW_{t(l)})\cap(f')^{-1}B,M)$ indexed by increasing $(p+1)$-tuples [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Assume these equivalences commute with restrictions of $B$, take multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_{T'})$ to multiplication by the restriction of $(f')^*b$ on each coordinate, and intertwine $d_K$ with the signed face-restriction sum. Let $D$ be a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves on $X'$. Suppose its terms, after forgetting to presheaves of global-ring modules, are identified by natural isomorphisms $e_p$ with the usual all-tuple Cech terms of $W,M$. Assume $e$ intertwines differentials, and each coordinate on an open $C\subset X'$ takes multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_{X'})$ to multiplication by its restriction to $(\bigcap_lW_{y(l)})\cap C$. Then $K$ is homotopy equivalent, as a complex of module sheaves on $T'$, to $f'_*D$ extended by zero to integer degrees. No covering assumption, augmentation, quasi-coherence, or affineness is required.

proof.text: For every open B of Tprime evaluate e on fprime inverse image B to identify pushforward D with all-tuple cochains of M. Identify categorical products of opens with intersections through the unique product isomorphisms, and replace ULift indices by their Fin values. Use a to identify K with increasing-tuple cochains. Naturality of e and hn give the restriction maps in these coordinates; hl and hlinear identify the local scalar actions. Restrict all-tuples to increasing-tuples to obtain the forward comparison. The chain-map equation follows from hd, ha and the matching signed face restrictions.

Define the reverse comparison by sorting each tuple: on a tuple with distinct entries, evaluate its sorted increasing coordinate and multiply by the sign of the sorting permutation; on a tuple with repeated entries put zero. All intersection transports are unique. The face sign equation checks the cochain-map identity: for distinct entries the deletion order gives exactly the signed sorted face; for repeated entries the only possibly nonzero deletions occur as a pair with opposite signs. Restriction after signed extension is identity on increasing coordinates.

For a p-tuple let sigma be its stable sorting permutation, and sigma_a the permutation agreeing with sigma before a and listing the remaining positions in their original order. The first degree-minus-one homotopy sums evaluations of the (p+1)-cochain on sigma(0),...,sigma(a),sigma_a(a),...,sigma_a(p), with coefficient (-1)^a sign(sigma_a). Expanding dh+hd pairs deletions off the junction with the same deletion in the adjacent summand, with opposite sign. The endpoints give identity minus signed stable sorting. This retracts onto semi-alternating cochains, identified with cochains indexed by nondecreasing tuples. There use the second homotopy: zero on increasing tuples; otherwise repeat the index at the first equality position a with coefficient (-1)^a. On expansion, deletions outside the duplicate pair cancel, leaving identity minus extension by zero from increasing tuples. Compose these homotopies to obtain the homotopy of the full-complex composite with identity; the increasing-complex composite is exactly identity.

Every formula uses only finite sums, integer signs, and coefficient restrictions between equal intersections. Thus it commutes with restriction of B, and is Gamma(B,O_Tprime)-linear, since the local scalar pulls back to the same coefficient open in each term. The coordinate maps and their inverses are natural and locally linear, so these formulas assemble into maps and homotopies of module sheaves. They extend to integer degrees by zero: hK gives zero negative K terms and D is extended by zero. The boundary homotopy equations use those zero terms and coincide with the natural-degree equations. Empty families give zero terms and unique maps. This yields the claimed homotopy equivalence.

theorem orderedCech_module_comparison {X' T' : Scheme.{u}} (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    (M : X'.Modules) {r : ℕ} (W₀ : ULift.{u} (Fin r) → X'.Opens)
    (K : CochainComplex T'.Modules ℤ) (hK : K.IsStrictlyGE 0)
    (a : ∀ (p : ℕ) (B : T'.Opens),
      Γ(K.X (p : ℤ), B) ≃+
        (∀ t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r,
          Γ(M, alternatingCechIntersection (fun i ↦ W₀ ⟨i⟩) t ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B)))
    (hn : ∀ (p : ℕ) {B C : T'.Opens} (i : B ⟶ C)
        (s : Γ(K.X (p : ℤ), C)) (t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r),
      a p B ((K.X (p : ℤ)).presheaf.map i.op s) t =
        M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf le_rfl
          ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f'.base).map i).le)).op (a p C s t))
    (hl : ∀ (p : ℕ) (B : T'.Opens) (b : Γ(T', B))
        (s : Γ(K.X (p : ℤ), B)) (t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r),
      a p B (b • s) t =
        X'.presheaf.map (homOfLE (show
          alternatingCechIntersection (fun i ↦ W₀ ⟨i⟩) t ⊓ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B ≤ f' ⁻¹ᵁ B
            from inf_le_right)).op (f'.app B b) • a p B s t)
    (ha : ∀ (p : ℕ) (B : T'.Opens) (s : Γ(K.X (p : ℤ), B))
        (t : Fin (p + 2) ↪o Fin r),
      a (p + 1) B ((K.d (p : ℤ) ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).app B s) t =
        ∑ j : Fin (p + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
          M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf
            (alternatingCechIntersection_face_le (fun i ↦ W₀ ⟨i⟩) p t j) le_rfl)).op
              (a p B s ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t)))
    (D : CochainComplex X'.Modules ℕ)
    (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          (D.X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor W₀).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X'.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj
              M.presheafModuleCat)).X p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (D.d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor W₀).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X'.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj
              M.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1))
    (hlinear : ∀ (p : ℕ) (y : Fin (p + 1) → ULift.{u} (Fin r)) (B : X'.Opens),
        let c : Γ(D.X p, B) → Γ(M, (∏ᶜ fun l ↦ W₀ (y l)) ⨯ B) :=
          fun s ↦ ((e p).hom ≫ Pi.π (fun y : Fin (p + 1) → ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦
            ((prod.functor (C := X'.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj
                M.presheafModuleCat).obj
                (op (∏ᶜ fun l ↦ W₀ (y l)))) y).app (op B) s
        ∀ (a : Γ(X', B)) (s : Γ(D.X p, B)),
          c (a • s) = X'.presheaf.map (prod.snd :
            (∏ᶜ fun l ↦ W₀ (y l)) ⨯ B ⟶ B).op a • c s) :
    Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv K
      ((((Modules.pushforward f').mapHomologicalComplex _).obj D).extend
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat))
